title: Musa and the Children of Israel
blurb: Egypt, Sinai and Jerusalem. The age of Musa, Dawud, Sulayman and Yunus, ending with exile in Babylon.

events.title: Shuayb and the traders
events.what: Shuayb tells the traders of Madyan to give full measure. They refuse and are destroyed by an earthquake.

events.title: Akhenaten's sun-disc
events.what: Pharaoh Akhenaten closes the old temples and orders worship of the Aten, the sun-disc, alone. After his death Egypt returns to its many gods.
events.tie: The believer of Pharaoh's family reminds Egypt that Yusuf had come to them before with clear proofs (40:34).
events.note: Sun worship is not tawhid. Whether older belief in one God shaped him is debated.

events.title: Musa in the river
events.what: Pharaoh kills newborn boys of Bani Israil. Musa's mother sets him in the river. Pharaoh's wife raises him in the palace.

events.title: Ramesses II
events.what: Ramesses II rules Egypt for 66 years, raising giant temples and a new capital in the Nile Delta.
events.tie: Many name him as the Pharaoh of Musa, but the Quran never names Pharaoh and scholars disagree.
events.note: Others propose his son Merneptah, or kings centuries earlier.

events.title: Musa flees to Madyan
events.what: Musa flees Egypt after an accidental killing, marries in Madyan and works there for ten years.

events.title: The fire at Tuwa
events.what: In the valley of Tuwa, Allah speaks to Musa, gives him the staff and the shining hand, and sends him with Harun to Pharaoh.

events.title: Musa before Pharaoh
events.what: Musa's staff swallows the magicians' tricks. The magicians believe. Plagues follow: locusts, lice, frogs, blood.

events.title: The believer of Pharaoh's family
events.what: A man of Pharaoh's own family, hiding his faith, speaks up: 'Do you kill a man because he says, My Lord is Allah?' He warns them of the nations before.

events.title: The first peace treaty
events.what: Fifteen years after the battle of Kadesh, Egypt and the Hittites sign the oldest surviving peace treaty. A copy hangs at the United Nations.
events.tie: The Quran says: 'If they incline to peace, then incline to it also' (8:61).

events.title: Haman's tower
events.what: Mocking Musa, Pharaoh tells Haman to fire bricks of clay and build a tower, so he can climb up and look at the God of Musa.
events.note: The Quran names Haman as Pharaoh's minister. Historians have not identified him.

events.title: Asiya's prayer
events.what: Pharaoh's wife believes in the Lord of Musa. Tormented for it, she prays for a house near Allah in Paradise. The Prophet ﷺ named her among the most perfect of women.
events.note: Her torment is described by the commentators. The Quran calls her 'the wife of Pharaoh'.

events.title: The sea parts
events.what: The sea splits for Bani Israil and closes on Pharaoh. His body is preserved as a sign.

events.title: The Tawrat and the calf
events.what: Musa spends forty nights on the mountain and receives the Tawrat. His people worship a golden calf while he is away.

events.title: The Samiri's calf
events.what: While Musa is away, the Samiri shapes the people's gold into a lowing calf. Harun warns them. Musa returns, burns the calf and scatters it in the sea.

events.title: Twelve springs
events.what: When his people thirst, Musa strikes a rock with his staff. Twelve springs gush out, one for each tribe, and clouds shade them.

events.title: The cow
events.what: Told to slaughter a cow, Bani Israil stall with question after question. A slain man is revived to name his killer.

events.title: Qarun
events.what: Qarun, rich beyond counting, boasts that he earned it all himself. The earth swallows him and his house.

events.title: Musa and al-Khidr
events.what: Musa travels to learn from al-Khidr. A boat holed, a boy killed, a wall rebuilt: each makes sense only at the end.

events.title: Forty years in the desert
events.what: Bani Israil refuse to enter the holy land. They wander forty years, fed with manna and quail.

events.title: The death of Musa
events.what: Harun dies in the wilderness, then Musa. Musa asks to be brought a stone's throw from the holy land, and is buried by a red sandhill.
events.note: Reported by al-Bukhari and Muslim. The shrine of Nabi Musa near Jericho is a later tradition.

events.title: 'Israel' in stone
events.what: Pharaoh Merneptah's victory stone names a people called Israel in Canaan. It is the oldest mention of Israel outside scripture.
events.tie: The Quran speaks of Bani Israil, the Children of Israil, dozens of times.

events.title: Into the holy land
events.what: After Musa, Yusha' leads a new generation into the holy land. Told to enter the gate humbly saying 'hittah', forgive us, some mock and change the word.
events.note: A hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim says the sun was held back for a prophet until a city fell; Ahmad's version names him as Yusha'.

events.title: The Olmec
events.what: In the forests of southern Mexico, the Olmec carve colossal stone heads and build the first great towns of Mesoamerica.
events.tie: The Quran says Allah made people into nations and tribes so they would know one another (49:13).

events.title: The Vedas
events.what: Hymns of the Rigveda, the oldest Hindu scripture, are composed in Sanskrit and passed down by memory for centuries.
events.tie: The Quran says there was no nation but that a warner had passed among them (35:24).
events.note: Dates for the Rigveda range from about 1500 to 1000 BCE.

events.title: The Bronze Age collapse
events.what: In a few decades the Hittite empire, Ugarit and Mycenaean Greece fall to drought, earthquakes and raiding Sea Peoples. Iron soon replaces bronze.
events.tie: 'These days We alternate among the people' (3:140): and iron, which the Quran says was sent down with great might (57:25), takes bronze's place.

events.title: The camel carries Arabia
events.what: In southern Arabia the camel is tamed for riding and carrying loads. Caravans can now cross deserts that were closed before.
events.tie: The Quran asks: 'Do they not look at the camels, how they are created?' (88:17)
events.note: Some date camel taming earlier; its use in long caravans spread around 1000 BCE.

events.title: The alphabet
events.what: Phoenician traders at Byblos and Tyre spread a short alphabet of 22 letters. Greek, Latin, Hebrew and Arabic letters all descend from it.
events.tie: The first revelation praises Allah 'who taught by the pen' (96:4); the Quran's own letters grew from this family.

events.title: The Mandate of Heaven
events.what: The Zhou overthrow the Shang and teach that Heaven gives rule to the just and takes it from the corrupt.
events.tie: The Quran says: 'You give sovereignty to whom You will and take it from whom You will' (3:26).

events.title: The Ark comes back
events.what: As a sign of Talut's kingship, the Ark of the Covenant returns, carried by angels. In it is reassurance from Allah and relics of the families of Musa and Harun.
events.note: Commentators say the relics included Musa's staff and pieces of the tablets.

events.title: Dawud and Jalut
events.what: Talut is made king. His small army is tested at a river. The young Dawud kills the giant Jalut.

events.title: The Sabbath-breakers
events.what: In a town by the sea, fish swarm on the Sabbath, when fishing is forbidden. Some trick the law; others warn them. Only the warners are saved.
events.note: Many commentators say the town was Aylah, today's Aqaba, in the time of Dawud. The Quran does not name it.

events.title: King Dawud
events.what: Dawud becomes king and prophet. He receives the Zabur, softens iron, and the mountains praise Allah with him.

events.title: Zoroaster
events.what: Zoroaster preaches a supreme Wise Lord against the forces of the lie. His faith becomes the religion of Persia's empires.
events.tie: The Quran names the Majus, the Zoroastrians, among the faiths Allah will judge between (22:17).
events.note: His dates range from about 1500 to 600 BCE, and his homeland is uncertain. Balkh is one tradition.

events.title: Luqman's advice to his son
events.what: Luqman the wise teaches his son: never associate anything with Allah, honour your parents, pray, be patient, and walk the earth humbly.
events.note: The Quran gives no time or place. Many commentators say he was a Nubian or Abyssinian sage of Dawud's time, not a prophet.

events.title: The field and the sheep
events.what: Sheep stray into a man's field at night and eat the crop. Dawud judges, young Sulayman finds a better ruling, and Allah praises both.

events.title: Sulayman's kingdom
events.what: Sulayman rules jinn, wind and birds. He builds the temple at Bayt al-Maqdis, the first qiblah.

events.title: The valley of the ants
events.what: Marching with his army, Sulayman hears an ant tell the others to hide. He smiles and prays to be grateful for Allah's favours.
events.note: Commentators place the valley in Sham or near Ta'if. No one knows.

events.title: Harut and Marut in Babylon
events.what: Devils spread magic and blame Sulayman. In Babylon, Harut and Marut teach it only as a test, first warning: 'We are a trial, so do not disbelieve.'

quote.from: It was not Solomon who disbelieved
quote.to: so do not disbelieve [by practicing magic].

events.note: Most scholars read them as angels sent as a test; some read them as men. Stories of their fall come from Isra'iliyyat and are weak.

events.title: The Queen of Sheba
events.what: The hoopoe reports a queen who worships the sun. Her throne is brought in a blink. The Queen of Sheba submits.

events.title: The staff and the termite
events.what: Sulayman dies leaning on his staff, and the jinn keep working. Only when a creature gnaws the staff and he falls do they see they never knew the unseen.

events.title: Ilyas against Baal
events.what: Ilyas calls his people away from the idol Baal. Al-Yasa continues his work.

events.title: Yunus and the whale
events.what: Yunus leaves Nineveh in anger and is swallowed by the whale. He repents. His city of 100,000 believes and is spared.

events.title: Rome is founded
events.what: By legend, Romulus founds Rome on the Tiber. The small town will one day rule Palestine and Egypt.
events.tie: Surah al-Rum (30:2-4) later foretells Rome's comeback against Persia.

events.title: The dam of Saba
events.what: The Sabaeans build a great dam at Marib to water two vast gardens. Saba grows rich on frankincense carried north by caravan.
events.tie: The Quran calls Saba's two gardens a sign, before the flood of the dam (34:15-16).
events.note: Older works stood here; the great dam was raised and repaired over a thousand years.

events.title: Homer
events.what: The Iliad and the Odyssey, long poems credited to Homer, are sung across the Greek world.
events.tie: Arabs too prized poetry above every art, which is why the Quran's challenge to make one surah like it (2:23) struck so hard.

events.title: The Black Pharaohs
events.what: Kings of Kush, from Nubia in today's Sudan, conquer Egypt and rule it as pharaohs for nearly a century.
events.tie: The Quran counts 'the diversity of your languages and your colours' among Allah's signs (30:22).

events.title: Assyria exiles Israel
events.what: Assyria takes Samaria and deports the ten northern tribes of Israel across its empire. They vanish from history as tribes.
events.tie: The Quran reminds Bani Israil that Allah's help was tied to keeping His covenant (5:12-13).

events.title: Nineveh falls
events.what: Babylon and the Medes destroy Nineveh. The Assyrian empire ends.
events.tie: Tradition makes Nineveh the city of Yunus, whose people believed and were spared punishment (10:98), long before Babylon brought it down.

events.title: The first coins
events.what: Lydia, in western Anatolia, strikes the first coins. Money spreads through the Greek and Persian worlds.
events.tie: The Quran mentions dirhams in Yusuf's story (12:20) and warns those who give short measure (83:1-3).

events.title: Exile to Babylon
events.what: Babylon burns the temple and takes Bani Israil into exile. Many scholars read this as the first punishment in Surah al-Isra.
events.tie: The Quran says that for the first of two corruptions Allah sent 'servants of Ours - those of great military might' into their homes (17:5).

events.title: A hundred years asleep
events.what: A man passes the ruined city and asks how it can live again. Allah makes him die a hundred years, then revives him. Many say he was Uzayr.
